$comment: Credential-shaped LITERALS in chart values that are acknowledged, not yet minted.
All five are the SAME credential: seaweedfs declares the S3 identity, and loki plus
mimir x3 present it back. That is the entire population -- the first scan of every
Application valuesObject and every bootstrap valuesContent across the cluster surface
found five, and no others. So this audit is a floor at ZERO the moment
081M1S6Z5S3087G0R000GEPSS2 lands, and until then it closes the class against NEW
literals rather than waiting for the migration.
They are acknowledged rather than fixed because the fix is not divisible: the producer
and all three consumers must agree on one value, and `applyDevBootstrapSecrets` draws
fresh entropy PER SPEC, so three namespaces cannot share a minted secret today. Changing
any one file alone would leave a service authenticating with a key the store does not know.
NO ENTRY QUOTES THE SECRET. The audit does not print values either -- a check that reports
a committed credential by quoting it has copied it into every CI log that runs the check.

entries.reason: THE PRODUCER. seaweedfs declares the S3 identity that loki and mimir authenticate as, so this literal is the ROOT of the group -- the other four are consumers presenting the same string back. Rendering the chart confirms it is live rather than decorative: it lands in the rendered Secret twice, as `admin_secret_access_key` and again inside the `seaweedfs_s3_config` identities JSON. Minting it is the whole of 081M1S6Z5S3087G0R000GEPSS2 and it cannot be done here, because the producer and all three consumers must agree on ONE value and `applyDevBootstrapSecrets` draws fresh entropy PER SPEC.
entries.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN: this exact coordinate stops holding a literal -- an empty value, a `${ENV}` reference, or an existingSecret indirection all satisfy it. The key is file+path, so MOVING the credential retires the entry automatically and the audit reports a key matching nothing as STALE; a fix cannot quietly leave its excuse behind. All five retire together under 081M1S6Z5S3087G0R000GEPSS2, because the producer and the three consumers must agree on one minted value.

entries.reason: A CONSUMER of the seaweedfs literal above, presenting it to reach loki-chunks and loki-ruler. Cannot move before the producer does: swapping this one to a minted value alone would leave loki authenticating with a key the blob store does not know. The consumer side additionally needs `-config.expand-env=true` plus an env var from a secretKeyRef, which is the unmeasured half named in the work-item.
